text:
FIRST VOICE

The waves have a faint harmony;
the violets, a gentle scent;
the cold night, mists of silver;
the day, light and gold;
I have something better:
I have Love.

SECOND VOICE

A breeze of applause, a radiant cloud,
a wave of envy kissing one's feet,
an island of dreams where the yearning
soul may rest,
a sweet intoxication:
that is Glory.

THIRD VOICE

Treasure is a burning coal,
vanity a fleeing shadow;
all is false: glory, gold.
What I adore
alone is true:
Liberty.

So the boatmen passed, singing
the eternal song,
and foam leapt at each stroke of the oar
and the sun struck it.

“Will you come aboard?” they cried. And I, smiling,
said to them as they passed:
“I did so long ago; indeed I still have
my clothes spread out to dry on the shore.”

translation.title: Rhyme LXXII: The Waves Have a Faint Harmony
translation.editorial_note: Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
